'''''Lysimachia nummularia''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the primrose [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Primulaceae]]. Its [[common name]]s include '''moneywort''', '''creeping jenny''',{{efn|This name also sometimes refers to ''[[Lysimachia congestiflora]]''.}} '''herb twopence''' and '''twopenny grass'''.<ref name=RHSPF>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/10632/Lysimachia-nummularia/Details |title=''Lysimachia nummularia'' |publisher=RHS |access-date=28 June 2021 }}</ref>

==Description==
It is a vigorous, prostrate, [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|5|cm|0|abbr=on}} in height and spreading rapidly and indefinitely by stem-rooting. It has rounded leaves arranged in opposite pairs, and cup-shaped yellow flowers 2 cm in diameter, in summer. It is particularly associated with damp or even wet areas, though in cultivation it will tolerate drier conditions.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1-4053-3296-5|pages=1136}}</ref> It is [[Hardiness (plants)|hardy]], surviving lows of {{convert|-15|C|F|abbr=on}} (RHS H5).<ref name=RHSPF/>

==Distribution==
It is native to Europe, but has been introduced to North America, where it is considered an invasive species in some areas.<ref name=invasive.org>{{cite web |title=Weed of the Week: Moneywort |url=https://www.invasive.org/weedcd/pdfs/wow/monewart.pdf |website=Invasive and Exotic Species of North America |access-date=11 May 2025}}</ref> It aggressively spreads in favorable conditions, such as low wet ground or near ponds. It can be weeded by hand, if all stems and stem fragments are removed, to prevent the stems from rooting and regrowing.<ref name="invasive.org"/>

==Etymology==
The Latin [[specific epithet]] ''nummularia'' means "like a coin",<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1-84533-731-5|pages=224}}</ref> referring to the shape of the leaves; hence the common names, such as "moneywort", which also references coins.

==Cultivation==
The cultivar 'Aurea' (golden creeping Jenny) has yellow leaves, and is somewhat less aggressive than the undomesticated species. It is cultivated as an ornamental plant, for [[groundcover]] where the range of its growth can be limited. It is also suitable as a [[bog garden]] or aquatic marginal plant.<ref name=MBG>{{cite web |url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=t120 |title=''Lysimachia nummularia'' 'Aurea' |publisher=[[Missouri Botanical Garden]] |access-date=11 July 2021}}</ref> It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/47321/Lysimachia-nummularia-Aurea/Details |title=''Lysimachia nummularia'' 'Aurea' |publisher=RHS |access-date=28 June 2021 }}</ref>
